headline: Red Wings’ John Gibson leaves game with upper-body injury
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Detroit goalie John Gibson left the Red Wings' game against the Canucks with an upper-body injury and did not return.

The timing stings because Gibson's year has been shaky. So far this season he has a .873 save percentage over six games and sits 1.7 goals below what an average goalie would have saved on the same shots (goals saved above expected). Last season he was 10.11 goals better than expected over 57 games, so this looks like a slow start more than a new baseline. Detroit has still been decent in front of him: the team is 3-3-3 with 49.7 percent of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality), and the team's goalies have saved 3.5 goals more than expected overall. The bigger issue is finishing, with the Wings 7.1 goals below expected scoring. If Gibson misses time, Detroit's even-strength play (51 percent of expected goals at five-on-five) is good enough to stay in games, but the goaltending cushion thins. Fantasy managers holding Gibson should check for updates before locking lineups.
